In 1975, approximately 700 acres of Tract II and 1,575 acres of Tract III were in active crop cultivation. In addition there are 985 acres in Tract II and 680 acres in Tract III which have been used for crop production in the past but are now either abandoned or reseeded to grass. The income and feed derived from this land is used to supplement the basic industry of the area which is livestock.
The average value of grazing land in the area is $90-$100/acre.

Dry farmland averages $200-$350/acre depending on its location, rainfall and other factors. These estimates are based upon current figures quoted by agricultural representatives of the Big Horn County State Bank and the Little Big Horn County State Bank.
Present mining plans for Tract III indicate that 2,151 acres will actually be disturbed in the next 20 years. Approximately 1,000 acres of land presently being farmed will be mined at that time.
Dames and Moore (1975) investigated for Westmoreland Resources the lands on Tracts II and III to evaluate those lands with an irrigation potential. The results of this study are given in Table II-28 and show the amount of land within each tract by potential. Class 1 lands are those with a high productivity value, Class 2 lands are intermediate value while Class 3 lands are the lowest value suitable for irrigation.
